canonical.title: See — Singapore: the unmissable icons + heritage to see (first-visit guide)

siblings.title: Eat Singapore: A First-Visit Food Guide for a Ghent Couple
siblings.summary: Where to eat your way through Singapore's hawker legends, crab feasts, Peranakan-Indian-Malay-Chinese threads, and offbeat supper spots on a first visit.

siblings.title: Sleep — Singapore: Character Stays for a First Visit
siblings.summary: Character over category: shophouse, design, heritage and treehouse stays across Singapore's six base neighbourhoods, plus the one first-visit icon — with EUR/night bands and angle tags.

siblings.title: Do — Singapore: semi-adventurous activities for a first visit
siblings.summary: Trek-light, kayak, cycle, swim and snorkel-light dos around Singapore — difficulty, guide-need and half/full-day for each, plus activity-led day-trips.

siblings.title: Offbeat Singapore: The Weird Stuff a First-Timer Misses
siblings.summary: A themed field guide to Singapore's strangest corners — hells, ghost reservoirs, last villages, leaning mosques and dragon kilns — far from the obvious icons.

siblings.title: Culture in Singapore: a first-visit guide to museums, festivals & crafts
siblings.summary: What cultural sights, festivals and workshops to plan a first Singapore trip around — marquee and offbeat, tagged by location and dated for 2026.

siblings.title: Around & day-trips — Singapore (first-visit guide)
siblings.summary: Changi-to-city options, getting around by MRT/Grab, and the day-trip orbit (Pulau Ubin, southern islands, Johor Bahru, Bintan) with times and EUR prices.

sources.title: Gardens by the Bay — entrance fees
sources.claim: Gardens by the Bay 2026 prices: two conservatories S$46 non-resident adult; outdoor gardens free; both domes must be visited same day; Supertree Observatory ~S$14, closed 11 Jun 2026.

sources.title: Cloud Forest — Gardens by the Bay
sources.claim: Cloud Forest houses a 35 m indoor waterfall in a misty mountain, with Avatar: The Experience zones.

sources.title: Flower Dome — Gardens by the Bay
sources.claim: Flower Dome shows seasonal floral displays including Tulipmania 24 Apr–17 May 2026.

sources.title: Free light shows — Singapore Gardens & Marina Bay
sources.claim: Garden Rhapsody is free at Supertree Grove 19:45 & 20:45; Spectra is free at MBS 20:00/21:00 daily plus 22:00 Fri-Sat.

sources.title: Garden Rhapsody — Gardens by the Bay
sources.claim: Garden Rhapsody is the free nightly light-and-sound show at Supertree Grove.

sources.title: SkyPark Observation Deck — Marina Bay Sands
sources.claim: MBS SkyPark Observation Deck sits ~200 m up for skyline views; timed entry.

sources.title: MBS SkyPark tickets — Traveloka
sources.claim: SkyPark 2026 adult ticket S$35 non-peak, S$39 peak (sunset); tickets are timed.

sources.title: Spectra — Marina Bay Sands
sources.claim: Spectra is a free nightly outdoor light-and-water show at the MBS Event Plaza.

sources.title: Merlion Park guide — NRI Travelogue
sources.claim: Merlion Park is free and open 24/7; best photographed before 9am or after 7pm; framed against Marina Bay Sands.

sources.title: Merlion Park history & photo tips — Travjoy
sources.claim: The Merlion statue stands 8.6 m tall, built 1972 by Lim Nang Seng.

sources.title: HSBC Rain Vortex — Jewel Changi Airport
sources.claim: The HSBC Rain Vortex at Jewel Changi is the world's tallest indoor waterfall at 40 m and is free to view.

sources.title: Jewel Changi Canopy Park tickets — A Globe Well Travelled
sources.claim: Most of Jewel is free (Rain Vortex, Forest Valley, Level 5); a nightly light show runs from 20:00; only Canopy Park play attractions are ticketed.

sources.title: Canopy Park — Jewel Changi Airport
sources.claim: Canopy Park (Level 5) is ticketed and includes the 23 m Mastercard Canopy Bridge over the Rain Vortex, mazes and slides.

sources.title: Singapore Botanic Gardens — NParks
sources.claim: Singapore Botanic Gardens is free and open 05:00 to midnight daily, except the National Orchid Garden.

sources.title: Singapore Botanic Gardens — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Singapore Botanic Gardens was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2015 — the first tropical and Singapore's only such site.

sources.title: National Orchid Garden 60,000 orchids — NParks
sources.claim: The National Orchid Garden holds over 60,000 orchids, one of the world's largest tropical orchid displays.

sources.title: Botanic Gardens budget guide 2026
sources.claim: National Orchid Garden 2026 adult admission is about S$5.

sources.title: Singapore Flyer — Introducing Singapore
sources.claim: Singapore Flyer is a 165 m observation wheel with a 30-minute rotation in glass capsules.

sources.title: Is the Singapore Flyer worth it? — A Globe Well Travelled
sources.claim: Singapore Flyer adult S$40 vs MBS SkyPark S$35; SkyPark is higher, open-air and you can stay as long as you like, so it wins for first-timers.

sources.title: Future World — ArtScience Museum
sources.claim: ArtScience Museum's teamLab Future World needs a timed-entry ticket; selected zones unavailable 15 Jun–28 Aug 2026.

sources.title: ArtScience Museum tickets — Traveloka
sources.claim: ArtScience Museum admission runs roughly S$23 for adults.

sources.title: National Gallery Singapore tickets — Traveloka
sources.claim: National Gallery Singapore tickets ~S$14–20; it sits between City Hall and the former Supreme Court; Supreme Court wing galleries close from 1 Apr 2026.

sources.title: Civic District area guide — Let's Explore Singapore
sources.claim: The Civic District concentrates colonial sights — City Hall, old Supreme Court, National Gallery, Raffles Hotel, St Andrew's Cathedral (free, 9-16:00).

sources.title: Raffles Hotel Singapore — about
sources.claim: Raffles Hotel is a preserved colonial landmark in the civic district, free to walk through.

sources.title: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple — Visit Singapore
sources.claim: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple in Chinatown is a five-storey temple with free entry, near Sri Mariamman Temple.

sources.title: Guide to Buddha Tooth Relic Temple — Traveloka
sources.claim: Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is free, open daily 07:00-19:00, with a modest dress code (shoulders and knees covered; sarongs lent).

sources.title: Thian Hock Keng Temple — Visit Singapore
sources.claim: Thian Hock Keng is Singapore's oldest Chinese (Hokkien) temple, dedicated to sea-goddess Mazu.

sources.title: Thian Hock Keng Temple — Chinatown.sg
sources.claim: Thian Hock Keng (1839-42) was built without nails and is free to enter; the Chinatown Heritage Centre is at 48 Pagoda St.

sources.title: Little India visitor itinerary — HomeJourney
sources.claim: Little India's sights include Tekka Centre wet market and the colourful Tan Teng Niah villa.

sources.title: Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple — Evendo
sources.claim: Sri Veeramakaliamman Temple (Serangoon Rd) is dedicated to Kali with an ornate gopuram; free, open ~08:00-12:00 & 16:00-21:00, modest dress.

sources.title: Arab Street & Kampong Glam guide — Passport and Stamps
sources.claim: Kampong Glam's top sights are the Sultan Mosque, Arab Street and Haji Lane; visit ~08:00 for empty streets.

sources.title: Sultan Mosque — Visit Kampong Gelam
sources.claim: Sultan Mosque is free with a modest dress code (shoulders/knees covered; free robes lent); avoid Friday 11:00-14:00 prayers.

sources.title: Tiong Bahru walking trail — Ostrich Trails
sources.claim: Tiong Bahru is Singapore's first public-housing estate (1936-41), an Art Deco quarter with rounded corners and three Yip Yew Chong heritage murals.

sources.title: Hell's Museum — Haw Par Villa
sources.claim: Hell's Museum at Haw Par Villa is S$20 adult / S$10 kid, 10:00-18:00; park partially closed for works from 8 Dec 2025 but Museum stays open.

sources.title: Haw Par Villa — HoneyKids Asia
sources.claim: Haw Par Villa itself is free, an outdoor park of 1,000+ statues and 150 dioramas of Chinese folklore.

sources.title: Southern Ridges & Henderson Waves — Once in a Lifetime Journey
sources.claim: The Southern Ridges is a ~10 km elevated trail connecting four parks including Mount Faber and Telok Blangah Hill.

sources.title: Southern Ridges — TheSmartLocal
sources.claim: Henderson Waves is Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge at 36 m, free to walk, with panoramic city views.

sources.title: MacRitchie TreeTop Walk — TheSmartLocal
sources.claim: MacRitchie TreeTop Walk is a free 250 m canopy-level suspension bridge; best in early morning to avoid heat.

sources.title: Central Catchment hiking — NParks
sources.claim: TreeTop Walk is open Tue-Fri 09:00-17:00, Sat-Sun/PH 08:30-17:00, closed Mondays.

sources.title: Pulau Ubin day-trip guide — HomeJourney
sources.claim: Pulau Ubin holds Singapore's last kampong; the bumboat from Changi Point costs ~S$4 each way and departs once 12 passengers board.

sources.title: Visit Pulau Ubin — NParks
sources.claim: Pulau Ubin is an NParks-managed island reachable by bumboat from Changi Point Ferry Terminal.

sources.title: Pulau Ubin & Chek Jawa — Jasmine Alley
sources.claim: Pulau Ubin's Chek Jawa wetlands has a boardwalk and Jejawi Tower; the guided pontoon tour is suspended early 2026 but boardwalks stay open 07:00-19:00.

sources.title: Sentosa — official site
sources.claim: Sentosa offers free sights and a free beach shuttle tram serving Palawan, Siloso and Tanjong beaches.

sources.title: Sentosa — Wikipedia
sources.claim: Sentosa's Fort Siloso Skywalk is free; Palawan Beach has a suspension bridge to the 'southernmost point of continental Asia'.

sources.title: Singapore Cable Car — Mount Faber Leisure
sources.claim: Singapore Cable Car round-trip Sky Pass is S$35 adult (both Mount Faber and Sentosa lines), offering a 360° harbour view.

sources.title: Singapore Cable Car — Sentosa
sources.claim: The cable car links Mount Faber to Sentosa with aerial skyline views.

sources.title: Lazarus Island — Island Cruise
sources.claim: Lazarus Island (quiet beach) is reached by ferry to St John's Island then a causeway walk; book ahead on busy weekends.

sources.title: Best time to visit Singapore — Highlights Travel
sources.claim: Best weather is roughly Feb-Apr and Jun-Sep; the wet NE monsoon Nov-Jan brings ~19 rain days/month in short evening storms.
